rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Recursively merging a user-controlled object into another object can allow an attacker to modify the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.
Allowing writes to arbitrary properties of an object may lead to denial-of-service attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')
rules.description: Building an XPath expression from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious code by the user.
Accessing paths influenced by users can allow an attacker to access unexpected resources.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')
rules.description: Building a database query from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious code by the user.
If an object literal has two properties with the same name, the second property overwrites the first one, which makes the code hard to understand and error-prone.
Middleware with case-sensitive paths do not protect endpoints with case-insensitive paths.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Using uncontrolled stored values in HTML allows for a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability.
Misconfiguration of CORS HTTP headers allows for leaks of secret credentials.

rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.
Allowing writes to arbitrary properties of an object may lead to denial-of-service attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs ('XML Entity Expansion')
rules.description: Parsing user input as an XML document with arbitrary internal entity expansion is vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks.
Middleware with case-sensitive paths do not protect endpoints with case-insensitive paths.

rules.description: Building an XPath expression from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious code by the user.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
rules.description: Using user-controlled data as arguments to some commands, such as git clone, can allow arbitrary commands to be executed.
Accessing paths influenced by users can allow an attacker to access unexpected resources.
